insights.concise_text: Morphological segmentation with morfessor 2.0 and Tamil annotation data improved BLEU precision values in the RNNMorph model for agglutinative Tamil.

triple.subject: morphological segmentation with morfessor 2.0 and Tamil annotation data
triple.object: BLEU precision values in the RNNMorph model

insights.concise_text: The word2vec embeddings trained on 569,772 Tamil sentences slightly increased BLEU scores when used to refine the baseline RNNSearch system.

triple.subject: word2vec embeddings trained on 569,772 Tamil sentences
triple.object: BLEU scores of the baseline RNNSearch system

insights.concise_text: The phrase-based SMT system used the same corpus and 569,772 monolingual Tamil sentences for its language model, yet performed inferior to RNNSearch.

triple.subject: phrase-based SMT system using the same corpus and 569,772 monolingual Tamil sentences
triple.object: RNNSearch model

insights.concise_text: The structural discordance between English and Tamil sentences motivated global attention in the Bahdanau et al. Bahdanau2014 attention-based translation model.

triple.subject: structural discordance between English and Tamil sentences
triple.object: global attention in the Bahdanau et al. Bahdanau2014 attention-based translation model

insights.concise_text: The scarce Tamil parallel corpus and neural translation models' heavy corpus requirement jointly make English–Tamil neural MT especially difficult.

triple.subject: scarce Tamil parallel corpus and heavy corpus requirement of neural translation models
triple.object: English–Tamil neural MT

insights.concise_text: The trade-off between domain specificity and corpus size was addressed by selecting 197,792 sentences from different corpora across various domains.

triple.subject: trade-off between domain specificity and size of the corpus
triple.object: 197,792 sentences from different corpora across various domains

insights.concise_text: The RNNMorph model's unrestricted Tamil vocabulary of 41,906 words follows from morphological segmentation splitting words into morphemes.

triple.subject: morphological segmentation splitting words into morphemes
triple.object: RNNMorph model's unrestricted Tamil vocabulary of 41,906 words

insights.concise_text: The RNNMorph bucketing scheme increased every target sentence bucket count by 5 because the model involved morphs instead of words.

triple.subject: RNNMorph model involving morphs instead of words
triple.object: target sentence bucket count increased uniformly by 5

insights.concise_text: The BLEU score's micro-average precision computation limits interpretation of RNNMorph's large BLEU increase because morphological segmentation increases word units per sentence.

triple.subject: BLEU score's micro-average precision computation
triple.object: interpretation of RNNMorph's large BLEU increase

insights.concise_text: The extra monolingual Tamil corpus used for word2vec embedding and the phrase-based SMT language model is also described as 569,772 monolingual Tamil sentences.

triple.subject: extra monolingual Tamil corpus
triple.object: 569,772 monolingual Tamil sentences

insights.concise_text: Human evaluation on about 100 test-set sentences with 50 native annotators found RNNMorph better than RNNSearch + Word2Vec, supporting the BLEU-score increase as actual translation-performance improvement.

triple.subject: human evaluation on about 100 test-set sentences with 50 native annotators
triple.object: RNNMorph better than RNNSearch + Word2Vec

insights.concise_text: Morphological segmentation reduced the target vocabulary from 340,325 words to 41,906 morphs, and RNNMorph achieved saturation of perplexities much earlier than RNNSearch + Word2Vec.

triple.subject: morphological segmentation reducing the target vocabulary from 340,325 words to 41,906 morphs
triple.object: RNNMorph saturation of perplexities much earlier than RNNSearch + Word2Vec

insights.concise_text: The reduction in vocabulary size from 340,325 to 41,906 improved source sentence lookup, while RNNSearch with Word2Vec embeddings attended to EOS in the middle of sentences leading to incomplete translations.

triple.subject: reduction in vocabulary size from 340,325 to 41,906
triple.object: source sentence lookup compared with RNNSearch with Word2Vec embeddings

insights.concise_text: Morphological segmentation decreased the target vocabulary size but increased average sentence lengths, creating model complexity and more input units (morphs) per sentence for RNNMorph.

triple.subject: morphological segmentation
triple.object: decreased target vocabulary size and increased model complexity from more input units (morphs) per sentence

insights.concise_text: The increase in general sequence length from morphological segmentation is a proposed explanation for repetitions in some RNNMorph translations, which occur much less frequently in RNNSearch predictions.

triple.subject: increase in general sequence length from morphological segmentation
triple.object: repetitions in some RNNMorph translations

insights.concise_text: Morphological segmentation reduced unknown tokens compared with RNNSearch, and most Morph2Vec translation sentences have no INLINEFORM0 UNK INLINEFORM1 tokens.

triple.subject: morphological segmentation reducing unknown tokens compared with RNNSearch
triple.object: most Morph2Vec translation sentences having no INLINEFORM0 UNK INLINEFORM1 tokens

insights.concise_text: The conclusion that machine translation involving morphologically rich languages should use morphological segmentation is supported by RNNMorph being consistently better in perplexity values through the time steps.

triple.subject: RNNMorph consistently better in perplexity values through the time steps
triple.object: machine translation involving morphologically rich languages should use morphological segmentation

insights.concise_text: The model implemented in this paper only includes source-side morphological segmentation, so a morphological generator is essential for an end-to-end translation system because output units cannot be morphemes.

triple.subject: source-side morphological segmentation without target side morphological agglutination
triple.object: a morphological generator for an end-to-end translation system

insights.concise_text: Attention models developed to ensure correctness of translation of long sequences can address the increased model complexity from longer average sentence lengths caused by morphological segmentation.

triple.subject: attention models developed to ensure correctness of translation of long sequences
triple.object: increased model complexity from longer average sentence lengths caused by morphological segmentation

insights.concise_text: The static context vector drawback of early RNN Encoder Decoder models is addressed by the attention mechanism, which the paper uses in comparing RNNSearch with Word2Vec embedding and RNNMorph attention vectors.

triple.subject: attention mechanism
triple.object: early RNN Encoder Decoder models with static context vectors
